title: Optimize auto-tuner incident: resilience playbook, mitigations, and follow-up
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a weekend rollout of the Optimize auto-tuner (which suggests batching and KV cache config changes to reduce per-token cost), we introduced an automated config apply that misclassified a set of high-latency routes as safe-to-batch. The change caused request amplification and elevated tail latency (~95th-99th percentile) for affected customers, and in one case caused a customer-visible error spike. This ticket captures the post-incident analysis, immediate mitigations, and a concrete playbook for safe config apply/rollback in future tuning runs.

Scope & impact:
- Affected customers: 3 mid-market tenants using dedicated capacity with strict latency SLOs.
- Duration: March 1 00:12 UTC — March 1 02:05 UTC (incident window).
- Symptoms: higher 95th/99th latency, elevated queue lengths on serving pools, increased error rates for long-context chat sessions.

Root cause (short):
- The auto-tuner batch-safety classifier had a blind spot for routes with rare long-prefix KV cache hits. The classifier assigned a safe_batch=true label without detecting the bimodal latency distribution, leading the runtime to include those requests in larger batching groups. Batching increased scheduling jitter and created contention for limited GPU slots under the dedicated pools' autoscaling constraints.

Contributing factors:
- No canary window was used for config apply across dedicated pools; a single rollout pushed the config to all reserved nodes for the region.
- Rollback tooling existed but required manual approval and a multi-step operator job (too slow during incident).
- Monitoring dashboards lacked an explicit 'batching-impact' alert that correlates batching_rate with 95th latency per route.
- The safety tests used in CI did not include synthetic bimodal latency traces.

Timeline (key events):
- 2026-03-01 00:10 UTC — Auto-tuner scheduled apply for region-us-west-2 (batching config changes).
- 2026-03-01 00:12 UTC — Config pushed to Dedicated pool A (full rollout).
- 00:18 UTC — Increased queue depth and 95th latency observed on dashboards; incident declared at 00:22 UTC.
- 00:28 UTC — Engineering oncall rolled partial mitigation: limit batch size on affected pool; limited effect.
- 01:00 UTC — Identified classifier false-positive pattern; prepared rollback.
- 01:08 UTC — Manual rollback initiated; took ~20 minutes to propagate and clear queued work.
- 02:05 UTC — Metrics returned to baseline; incident closed for business impact.

Immediate mitigations applied during incident:
- Emergency override: disabled auto-apply for Optimize for all dedicated pools (global flag).
- Reduced maximum batch size per-pool to earlier safe config to drain queue depth quickly.
- Increased autoscale headroom temporarily (burst nodes) for affected dedicated pools to absorb backlog.

Longer-term fixes (planned):
1) Safety improvements to auto-tuner
   - Add a bimodal-latency detector to classifier training and inference.
   - Enforce a latency-sensitivity feature flag per-route used during suggestions.
   - Add conservative defaults for rare-route exposures (e.g., require >= 2x confidence).
2) Rollout & canary model changes
   - Canary window: apply changes to 1 node in pool, monitor for 30 minutes, then gradually expand.
   - Automatic staged rollback on threshold breach of correlating metrics.
3) Runbook, tooling, and observability
   - Playbook below (section).
   - Add a batching-impact alert: triggers when batching_rate increases > 30% and 95th latency increases > 20% in 10 minutes for a route.
   - Add synthetic CI traces with bimodal latency to safety harness.
4) Fast rollback tooling
   - Develop one-click rollback that reverts last auto-apply and cancels queued tasks; integrate with Console and oncall UI.

Playbook: Optimize auto-tuner apply/rollback (for oncall and infra owners)
- Pre-apply checklist (automated):
  - Verify model suggestions include confidence score and latency-sensitivity tag.
  - Ensure target pool has canary slot available (pool config: canary_slots >= 1).
  - Ensure autoscale headroom >= 10% for the region for 1 hour after apply.
  - Baseline snapshot: save current batching_rate, 95th latency, queue_depth per-route to snapshot storage.
- Canary apply (automated):
  - Apply to canary node; start 30-minute monitor window.
  - Monitor: batching_rate, 50/95/99 latency, queue_depth, GPU_util, and errors.
  - If batching_rate up > 30% AND 95th latency up > 20% OR errors > baseline+0.5%, abort and rollback.
- Gradual rollout (automated with human-in-loop):
  - Expand to 10% of nodes for 15 minutes, then 30%, then 100% if safe thresholds not breached.
  - Each stage requires automated health-check pass; if fail, stop and rollback.
- Fast rollback steps (one-click manual):
  - Click 'Revert last apply' in Console or run CLI: redwood optimize rollback --apply-id <id> --fast.
  - System marks routes as 'do-not-auto-apply' for 2h while reverting metrics settle.
  - Verify queue_depth and 95th latency decline to within 110% of baseline before re-enabling auto-apply.
- Post-rollback cleanup:
  - Re-run classifier diagnostics on affected routes; generate failure export and attach to ticket.
  - Create follow-up training job to incorporate false-positive examples.

Checklist for batching/caching recommendation safety (for Optimize engineers):
- Does the recommendation include a confidence score and exposed rationale? (yes/no)
- Does the route have long-tail sessions or bimodal latency traces in the last 30 days? (run detector)
- Is KV cache hit-rate > 80% for the sample window? If not, mark as 'cache-unsafe'.
- Are there rate-limited downstreams or external dependencies that amplify batching? (manual review)
- Simulate suggestion in a local load test with synthetic long-prefix KV patterns before apply.

Monitoring & alerts to implement:
- batching-impact alert (as above).
- apply-burst alert: when an automated apply changes > 10% of routes in a region within 10 minutes.
- rollback-failure alert: if a rollback doesn't reduce queue depth or latency in 30 minutes.
- console-ops card: show last apply id, stage, and owner on the region overview.

Action items (owners & deadlines):
- ENG/Optimize: implement bimodal detector + retrain classifier (owner: Liam Chen) — due 2026-03-22.
- ENG/Infra: one-click fast rollback CLI + Console integration (owner: Priya Nair) — due 2026-03-18.
- ENG/Observability: add batching-impact and apply-burst alerts, dashboard panels (owner: Mateo Alvarez) — due 2026-03-12.
- ENG/QA: add synthetic bimodal traces to CI safety tests (owner: Sanjay Rao) — due 2026-03-15.
- PM: update Optimize product docs and communication for customers about auto-tuner safe-rollout (owner: Morgan White) — due 2026-03-20.

Postmortem notes & discussion log (high level):
- 2026-03-02: PM review — agreed to freeze auto-apply for 48h and prioritize fast-rollback work.
- 2026-03-04: Design review — Console changes: add apply stage visibility and rollback CTA.
- 2026-03-06: RFC started for canary rollout automation.

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- One-click rollback implemented and tested in staging.
- Canary rollout automation merged and in Canary stage for one region.
- New alerts and dashboards live and validated.
- Classifier updated and CI safety traces added.

Notes about customer communication:
- Send affected customers a private incident summary with mitigation steps and what we changed to prevent recurrence (PM to own).
- Add a short public status note to status.redwood.ai referencing the incident and that auto-apply was temporarily disabled and then re-enabled after fixes.
